title: Arakhin 18
description: Why a witness need not stay fit from start to end, the leper whose father is dying or whose ship is leased, and a new mishna: the years follow the one valuated, the valuation is fixed at the time of the vow, the boundary year counts with the years below it, and which of the Torah’s years are counted from time to time.
topics: 👁️ “If he has seen … if he does not utter”: testimony depends on seeing and telling
⛵ A father on his deathbed and a leased ship: when is the leper still destitute?
⚖️ The years follow the one valuated, the sex follows the one valuated, the sum follows the time of the vow
💎 Assessments compared to valuations: a pearl for the poor, a limb by its significance
📏 The thirtieth day, the fifth, twentieth and sixtieth years count with the years below them
🔗 “Year”, “year”: a free verbal analogy, and Rabbi’s “until and including”
📅 Rabbi Eliezer’s extra month and a day
⏳ From time to time: offerings, walled cities, an ancestral field, a Hebrew slave, a son and a daughter

a1.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵתָה בִּתּוֹ, פִּקֵּחַ וְנִתְחָרֵשׁ וְחָזַר וְנִתְפַּקֵּחַ, פָּתוּחַ וְנִסְתַּמֵּא וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְפַּתֵּחַ, שָׁפוּי וְנִשְׁתַּטָּה וְחָזַר וְנִשְׁתַּפָּה — כָּשֵׁר. זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁתְּחִילָּתוֹ וְסוֹפוֹ בְּכַשְׁרוּת — כָּשֵׁר.

a2.he: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״אוֹ רָאָה... אִם לֹא יַגִּיד״, בִּרְאִיָּיה וְהַגָּדָה תְּלָא רַחְמָנָא מִילְּתָא, וְהָא אִיכָּא. וְאֶלָּא ״וְהוּא״ לְמָה לִי?

a3.he: לְכִדְתַנְיָא: רָאָה סִיאָה שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם עוֹמְדִין, וְעֵידָיו בֵּינֵיהֶן, וְאָמַר ״מַשְׁבִּיעַנִי עֲלֵיכֶם אִם יוֹדְעִים אַתֶּם לִי עֵדוּת שֶׁתָּבוֹאוּ וּתְעִידוּנִי״, יָכוֹל יְהוּ חַיָּיבִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״וְהוּא עֵד״, וַהֲרֵי לֹא יִיחֵד עֵידָיו.

a4.he: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ אָמַר ״כׇּל מִי״? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״וְהוּא עֵד״, וַהֲרֵי יִיחֵד עֵידָיו.

a5.he: אֲבָל בַּקׇּרְבָּנוֹת אֵינוֹ כֵּן וְכוּ׳. אָבִיו מֵת וְהִנִּיחַ לוֹ רִיבּוֹא — עָשִׁיר הוּא! אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, אֵימָא: מַנִּיחַ לוֹ רִיבּוֹא.

a6.he: פְּשִׁיטָא! כְּשֶׁהָיָה אָבִיו גּוֹסֵס. מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: רוֹב גּוֹסְסִין לְמִיתָה? קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a7.he: סְפִינָתוֹ בַּיָּם וּבָאָה לוֹ בְּרִיבּוֹאוֹת, עָשִׁיר הוּא! אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: כְּשֶׁהָיְתָה מוּחְכֶּרֶת וּמוּשְׂכֶּרֶת בְּיַד אֲחֵרִים. וְהָאִיכָּא שְׂכִירוּת? שְׂכִירוּת אֵינָהּ מִשְׁתַּלֶּמֶת אֶלָּא לְבַסּוֹף.

a8.he: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם סְפִינָה! הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא, דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיָה אִיכָּר — נוֹתֵן לוֹ צִמְדּוֹ, וְחַמָּר — נוֹתֵן לוֹ חֲמוֹרוֹ.

a9.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַשָּׁנִים בַּנִּידָּר, כֵּיצַד? יֶלֶד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ זָקֵן — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ זָקֵן, וְזָקֵן שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶת הַיֶּלֶד — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ יֶלֶד. הָעֲרָכִין בַּנֶּעֱרָךְ, כֵּיצַד? אִישׁ שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ הָאִשָּׁה — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ אִשָּׁה, וְאִשָּׁה שֶׁהֶעֱרִיכָה אִישׁ — נוֹתֶנֶת עֵרֶךְ אִישׁ.

a10.he: וְהָעֵרֶךְ בִּזְמַן הָעֵרֶךְ, כֵּיצַד? הֶעֱרִיכוֹ פָּחוּת מִבֶּן חָמֵשׁ, וְנַעֲשֶׂה יָתֵר עַל בֶּן חָמֵשׁ, פָּחוּת מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים, וְנַעֲשָׂה יָתֵר עַל בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים — נוֹתֵן בִּזְמַן הָעֵרֶךְ.

a11.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַתָּה הִקַּשְׁיתָּ דָּמִים לַעֲרָכִין, מַרְגָּלִית לְקַלִּים, וְלִידּוֹן בִּכְבוֹדוֹ.

a12.he: יָכוֹל נַקִּישׁ עֲרָכִין לְדָמִים, שֶׁיִּתֵּן כִּשְׁעַת נְתִינָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֵּן יָקוּם״, אֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן הָעֵרֶךְ.

a13.he: מַתְנִי׳ יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים כִּלְמַטָּה הֵימֶנּוּ, שְׁנַת חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים כִּלְמַטָּה מֵהֶם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִם מִבֶּן שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה״, הֲרֵי אָנוּ לְמֵדִים בְּכוּלָּן מִשְׁנַת שִׁשִּׁים, מָה שְׁנַת שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְמַטָּה הֵימֶנָּה, אַף שְׁנַת חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים כִּלְמַטָּה הֵימֶנָּה.

a14.he: הֵן? אִם עָשָׂה שְׁנַת שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְמַטָּה מִמֶּנָּה לְהַחְמִיר, נַעֲשֶׂה שְׁנַת חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים כִּלְמַטָּה מִמֶּנָּה לְהָקֵל?

a15.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״שָׁנָה״ ״שָׁנָה״ לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה, מָה שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה בִּשְׁנַת שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְמַטָּה, אַף שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה מִשְׁנַת חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים כִּלְמַטָּה מִמֶּנּוּ, בֵּין לְהָקֵל וּבֵין לְהַחְמִיר. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: עֵד שֶׁיְּהוּ יְתֵירוֹת עַל הַשָּׁנִים חֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד.

a16.he: גְּמָ׳ מוּפְנֶה, דְּאִי לָא מוּפְנֶה — אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ כִּדְפָרְכִינַן. ״שָׁנָה״ ״שָׁנָה״ יַתִּירָא כְּתִיבִי.

a17.he: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי, דְּאִי רַבִּי — הָאָמַר: ״עַד״ ״וְעַד״ בַּכְּלָל.

a18.he: דְּתַנְיָא: ״מִיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן וְעַד יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי״, יָכוֹל רִאשׁוֹן וְלֹא רִאשׁוֹן בַּכְּלָל, שְׁבִיעִי וְלֹא שְׁבִיעִי בַּכְּלָל,

b1.he: כָּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״מֵרֹאשׁוֹ וְעַד רַגְלָיו״, רֹאשׁוֹ וְלֹא רֹאשׁוֹ בַּכְּלָל, רַגְלָיו וְלֹא רַגְלָיו בַּכְּלָל?

b2.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עַד יוֹם הָאֶחָד וְעֶשְׂרִים לַחֹדֶשׁ בָּעָרֶב״. רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ, ״רִאשׁוֹן״ וְ״רִאשׁוֹן״ בַּכְּלָל, ״שְׁבִיעִי״ וּ״שְׁבִיעִי״ בַּכְּלָל!

b3.he: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי, שַׁקּוֹלֵי מְשַׁקְּלִי קְרָאֵי. מִכְּדֵי כְּתִיב: ״מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד בֶּן חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים״, תּוּ ״מִבֶּן חָמֵשׁ וְעַד בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים״ לְמָה לִי? הִילְכָּךְ אִישְׁתְּקִלוּ לְהוּ.

b4.he: אָמַר מָר: ״רֹאשׁוֹ״ — וְלָא רֹאשׁוֹ בַּכְּלָל, ״רַגְלָיו״ — וְלֹא רַגְלָיו בַּכְּלָל. מְנָלַן? אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: שָׁאנֵי סִימָנִים דְּגוּפוֹ מִסִּימָנִים דְּרֹאשׁוֹ. אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: ״לְכׇל מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן״.

b5.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ יְתֵירוֹת עַל הַשָּׁנִים חוֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד. תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״לְמַעְלָה״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״חֹדֶשׁ וָמַעְלָה״, מָה לְהַלָּן מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד, אַף כָּאן מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד.

b6.he: וְאֵימָא כִּי הָתָם, מָה הָתָם חַד יוֹמָא, אַף כָּאן חַד יוֹמָא? אִם כֵּן, גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה מַאי אַהֲנִי!

b7.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה בְּקָדָשִׁים, שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה בְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה, שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים שֶׁבִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, וְשֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים שֶׁבְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי, וְכֵן שֶׁבַּבֵּן וְשֶׁבַּבַּת — כּוּלָּן מֵעֵת לְעֵת.

b8.he: שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה בְּקָדָשִׁים, מְנָלַן? אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, אָמַר קְרָא: ״כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ״, שְׁנָתוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ, וְלֹא שֶׁל מִנְיַן עוֹלָם.

b9.he: שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה בְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה — דִּכְתִיב: ״עַד תֹּם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ״, מִמְכָּרוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ, וְלֹא שָׁנָה לְמִנְיַן עוֹלָם.

b10.he: שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים שֶׁבִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, דִּכְתִיב: ״בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר לָךְ״, פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם אוֹכֵל שָׁלֹשׁ תְּבוּאוֹת בִּשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים.

b11.he: שֵׁשׁ שֶׁבְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי — דִּכְתִיב: ״שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים יַעֲבֹד וּבַשְּׁבִיעִית״, זִימְנִין דְּבִשְׁבִיעִית נָמֵי יַעֲבוֹד.

b12.he: וְשֶׁבַּבֵּן וְשֶׁבַּבַּת כּוּלָּן מֵעֵת לְעֵת. לְמַאי הִילְכְתָא? אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב: לַעֲרָכִין. רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: לְפִרְקִין דְּ״יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן״.

b13.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: מִי פְּלִיגִיתוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, אֲנָא אֲמַרִי חֲדָא, וְהוּא אֲמַר חֲדָא. הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ פְּלִיגִי, מַאן דְּאָמַר לַעֲרָכִין לָא אָמַר לְ״יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן״? וְהָאָמַר רַב: הִילְכְתָא בְּכוּלֵּהּ פִּירְקָא מֵעֵת לְעֵת.

b14.he: וְאֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לַעֲרָכִין, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר לְ״יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן״? דּוּמְיָא דְּהָנָךְ, מָה הָנָךְ דִּכְתִיבָא, אַף הָנָךְ דִּכְתִיבָא.

b15.he: וְאִידַּךְ, אִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דִּכְתִיבָא, הַאי ״שֶׁבַּבֵּן וְשֶׁבַּבַּת״ —

messages.text: Continued from 17b: the Gemara asked why Rabbi Yehuda, who reads “and if he is poor” as poor from beginning to end, does not also read “and he is a witness” as requiring a witness to be fit from beginning to end. It cited a baraita: one who knew testimony and then became the party’s son-in-law, a deaf-mute, blind or an imbecile is disqualified; but if he knew testimony, then became his son-in-law,

and afterward his wife, who was the daughter of the father-in-law, died, which means that the witness is no longer related to the party involved; or when he was able to hear, and then became a deaf-mute, and again became able to hear; or when he could see, and subsequently became blind, and afterward could see again; or when he was halakhically competent, and then became an imbecile, and again became halakhically competent; in all these cases he is fit to testify.

notes.he: קודם שבא לב"ד להעיד:
notes.en: And afterward his daughter died: before he came to court to testify.

notes.he: שנתרחק:
notes.en: And his daughter died: so he became distant [no longer a relative].

messages.text: This is the principle: Any individual whose beginning and end is in a state of qualification to serve as a witness is qualified to testify, even if he was unfit in the interim.

notes.he: כל שתחלתו וסופו בכשרות כשר אע"פ שבנתיים היה פסול]:
notes.en: Whoever’s beginning and end are in a state of fitness is fit, even though he was unfit in between.

messages.text: Evidently, it is not derived from the verse: “And he is a witness,” that the witness must be fit from the beginning to the end.

The halakha is different there, with regard to testimony, as the verse states: “He is a witness, whether he has seen…if he does not utter”. This formulation indicates that the Merciful One renders the matter of testimony dependent on seeing and recounting the content of his testimony. And in this instance there is both valid seeing and valid recounting, despite the fact that the witness was disqualified in the interim.

verse.he: וְנֶפֶשׁ כִּי־תֶחֱטָא וְשָׁמְעָה קוֹל אָלָה וְהוּא עֵד אוֹ רָאָה אוֹ יָדָע אִם־לוֹא יַגִּיד וְנָשָׂא עֲוֺנוֹ׃
verse.en:
If a person incurs guilt—
When someone has heard a public imprecation but (although able to testify as having seen or learned of the matter) has not given information and thus is subject to punishment;

notes.he: בלבד שיהא ראוי בשעת ראיה ובשעת הגדה אע"ג דאיפסל בנתיים לא איכפת לן. [והא איכא. ראוי]:
notes.en: The Merciful One made it depend on seeing and telling: only that he be fit at the time of seeing and at the time of telling; even though he became unfit in between, we do not mind. [And there is: he is fit at both.]

messages.text: But if so, why do I need the exclusion of the verse: “And he is a witness”?

notes.dh: ואלא והוא ל"ל לרבי כדאית ליה ולרבנן כדאית להו
notes.he: וקשיא לרבי מאי דרשי רבנן (הכא הוא) ואם מך הוא מערכך ושמא יש דרשא בשום מקום מהאי הוא דהכא ודרשי' ליה:
notes.en: “But why do I need ‘he’? According to Rabbi, as he holds; according to the Rabbis, as they hold” [the Gemara’s answer on 17b about “and if he is poor”]: And it is difficult: what do the Rabbis expound from the “he” here, “But if he is too poor for your valuation” (Leviticus 27:8)? Perhaps there is an exposition of this “he” somewhere, and we expound it [from there].

notes.he: עד למה לי:
notes.en: “And he” is a witness: why do I need it?

messages.text: The limiting clause is necessary for that which is taught in a baraita:

If someone saw a crowd of people standing, and his witnesses were among them, and he said: I hereby administer an oath to you, if you know any testimony relating to me, that you will come and testify for me, one might have thought that this form of address suffices to single out the witnesses. This would mean that if the witnesses take a false oath that they do not know testimony with regard to the person who addressed them, they would be obligated to bring an offering of an oath of testimony.

notes.he: סיעה:
notes.en: Si’ah: [that is,] si’a, a group.

notes.he: העדים קרבן שבועת העדות אם לא העידוהו:
notes.en: One might have thought they would be liable: the witnesses, [to bring] the offering for an oath of testimony, if they did not testify for him.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “And he is a witness,” to emphasize that the offering applies only to one who is singled out as a witness, and in this case the individual did not single out his witnesses, as he addressed a whole crowd of people. Consequently, the witnesses are exempt.

notes.he: שהרי השביע את כולן:
notes.en: But he did not single out his witnesses: for he adjured all of them.

notes.he: [עד] שישמע העד ביחוד קול אלה ולא שישתתפנו עם אחרים:
notes.en: The verse states “and he is a witness”: [until] the witness hears the sound of the oath singled out [to him], and not that he joins him together with others.

messages.text: One might have thought that even if this individual said to the crowd: I adjure whoever knows testimony relating to me that he will come and testify for me, that even in the case of this more specific address the witnesses are likewise exempt from the offering of an oath of testimony.

notes.he: שיודע עדות אני משביע לא יהו חייבין:
notes.en: One might have thought that even if he said “whoever”: “Whoever knows testimony, I adjure him,” they would not be liable.

notes.he: כל מי מכם שיודע העדות יהא מושבע:
notes.en: One might have thought that even if he said “whoever”: “Whoever among you knows the testimony shall be under oath.”

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “And he is a witness,” and by clarifying his appeal the individual did single out his witnesses. Consequently, in this situation the witnesses would be obligated to bring the offering.

notes.dh: ת"ל והוא עד והרי ייחד עדיו
notes.he: שהרי לא השביע אלא עדיו:
notes.en: The verse states “and he is a witness,” and he did single out his witnesses: for he adjured only his witnesses.

notes.he: והרי ייחד עדיו שהרי עדיו השביע ולא אחרים:
notes.en: The verse states “and he is a witness,” and he did single out his witnesses: for he adjured his witnesses and not others.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: But with regard to the offerings of a leper that is not so. If the leper is destitute, even if his father died and left him ten thousand dinars, the Temple treasury has no share in it.

notes.he: שאם היה עני והעשיר אינו מביא קרבן עשיר:
notes.en: But with offerings it is not so: if he was poor and became rich, he does not bring a rich man’s offering.

notes.he: אלא אפילו מת אביו בשעה שהוא חייב להביא קרבן והניח לו ריבוא ליטרא או ספינתו בים ובאה לו בריבואות שכירות אין להקדש [בהן] כלום ומביא קרבן עני:
notes.en: Rather, even if his father died at the time he is obligated to bring the offering and left him ten thousand litra, or his ship is at sea and comes to him with tens of thousands in rent, the Temple treasury has nothing [in them], and he brings a poor man’s offering.

notes.he: מאי שנא בקרבנות דאין להקדש בהן כלום ומ"ש בערכין עני והעשיר דנותן ערך עשיר משום דבקרבנות כתיב אשר לא תשיג ידו בטהרתו אי משיג בזמן טהרה אין אי לא לא אבל בערכין כתיב כפי אשר תשיג יד הנודר יעריכנו הכהן אימתי שמשיג יתן ערך עשיר והא דאמרינן לקמן (דף כד.) שלא ישהא (אפילו) מרגליות לקלים כו' הני מילי כי לית ליה אבל כי אית ליה מידי ימתין ויתן ערך עשיר:
notes.en: What is different about offerings, where the Temple treasury has nothing in them, and what is different about valuations, where one who was poor and became rich gives a rich man’s valuation? Because with offerings it is written, “whose means do not suffice for his purification” (Leviticus 14:32): if he has the means at the time of purification, yes; if not, no. But with valuations it is written, “according to the means of him who vowed shall the priest valuate him” (Leviticus 27:8): whenever he has the means, he gives a rich man’s valuation. And what we say below (24a), that a pearl is not held back for the light [the poor], etc., applies only when he has nothing [else]; but when he has something, he waits and gives a rich man’s valuation.

messages.text: If his father already died and left him ten thousand dinars, he is wealthy. How could he be considered destitute at all?

notes.he: ואמאי אין להקדש כלום בהן:
notes.en: He is wealthy: so why does the Temple treasury have nothing of them?

notes.dh: אביו מת בשעת הבאת קרבן עשיר הוא
notes.he: אמאי מביא קרבן עני:
notes.en: His father died at the time of bringing the offering: then he is wealthy. Why does he bring a poor man’s offering?

messages.text: One should say instead: His father is dying and leaving him ten thousand dinars, but he has not yet died.

notes.he: שעדיין לא מת אביו אבל עתיד הוא להניח לו:
notes.en: Leaving: his father has not yet died, but he is going to leave it to him.

notes.he: כלומר לא תימא מת והניח לו שכבר באו לידו אלא מניח אביו [לו]:
notes.en: Say “leaving him”: that is, do not say “he died and left him,” so that it already came into his hands; rather, his father is leaving [it to him].

messages.text: If so, it is obvious that with regard to the Temple treasury he remains destitute, as at the time he is in fact destitute.
messages.quote: His father is dying and leaving him ten thousand dinars

notes.he: דהא לית ליה:
notes.en: It is obvious: for he does not have it.

notes.he: שאין להקדש כלום שעדיין לא הגיעו לידו:
notes.en: It is obvious: that the Temple treasury has nothing, since it has not yet reached his hands.

messages.text: The halakha was stated with regard to a case where his father is moribund. Lest you say that as the majority of moribund people proceed to die the son should be considered wealthy even before the father dies, the mishna therefore teaches us that the son retains his status as destitute until the father actually dies.

notes.he: בשעה שהכהן מעריכו:
notes.en: Where his father was moribund: at the time the priest valuates him.

notes.dh: לא צריכא שהיה אביו גוסס כו'
notes.he: פירש בקונט' אבל בערכין בדעת הכהן תליא רחמנא ואי חזי דאביו גוסס אינו מעריכו עד שימות אביו ולא נהירא דלקמן אמרינן אין בהקדש אלא מקומו ושעתו ובסמוך נמי מייתי לה אתה הקשת דמים לערכין ומרגלית לקלים פירוש עני שהעריך עצמו ויש לו מרגלית שאינה שוה עכשיו כי אם כ' סלעים אין אומרים נמתין עד שיבא יום השוק ותעלה לנ' סלעים אלא שמין אותה כמו שהיא עכשיו ולא יתן כ"א כ' סלעים וא"כ למה אנו צריכין להמתין עד שימות אביו לכן נראה לר"י דלא קאי אבל בקרבנות אינו כן אמת אביו אלא אהא דלעיל קאי וסוף מילתא דר' יהודה היא והא דמפרש אח"כ אפי' מת אביו והניח לו כו' מילתא באפי נפשה היא וקרבנות וערכין שוין בו:
notes.en: “It is necessary only where his father was moribund,” etc.: The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: but with valuations, the Merciful One made it depend on the priest’s judgment, and if he sees that the father is moribund, he does not valuate him until his father dies. This is not plausible, for below we say that the Temple treasury has only its place and its time; and just after this too the Gemara cites, “You compared assessments to valuations, and a pearl to the light,” meaning a poor man who valuated himself and has a pearl now worth only twenty sela: we do not say, “Let us wait until market day, when it will rise to fifty sela”; rather we assess it as it is now, and he gives only twenty sela. If so, why should we need to wait until his father dies? Therefore Ri holds that “but with offerings it is not so” does not refer to “his father died”; rather it refers to what was said before it, and it is the end of Rabbi Yehuda’s statement. And what is explained afterward, “even if his father died and left him,” etc., is a matter of its own, in which offerings and valuations are the same.

notes.he: וכמי דמת דמי שהגיע כבר לידו ועשיר הוא קמ"ל:
notes.en: [Lest you say] most moribund people go on to die: and it is as though he had died, so that it has already reached his hands and he is wealthy. It teaches us [that it is not so].

messages.text: The mishna likewise teaches: If his ship is at sea and merchandise valued at ten thousand dinars is coming into his possession, this money is not taken into consideration by the Temple treasury. But isn’t he wealthy?
The mishna is referring to a case where his ship was leased or rented to others, and therefore the merchandise it contains belongs to someone else.

notes.he: ספינתו מוחכרת ביד אחרים ואין לו בתוכה כלום אלא שכרה והיינו ריבוא דקתני במתני':
notes.en: Where it was [leased]: his ship was leased in the hands of others, and he has nothing in it except its rent; and that is the “ten thousand” the mishna speaks of.

notes.he: [חכירות] למחצית שכר או לשליש:
notes.en: [Where it was] leased: [leased] for half the profit or for a third.

messages.text: But isn’t there the rent money that will be paid to the leper?
messages.quote: his ship was leased or rented to others

messages.text: Rent is paid only at the end of the rental period, which means that the owner is destitute in the meantime.

notes.he: ועדיין לא הגיע לידו ולא הוי עשיר:
notes.en: Rent is [paid only at the end]: and it has not yet reached his hands, so he is not wealthy.

messages.text: But let the mishna derive and determine that the leper is wealthy due to the fact that he owns a ship.

notes.he: גופה שהיא שלו והוי עשיר]:
notes.en: [But let him derive it due to the ship: the ship itself, which is his, so he is wealthy.]

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this statement in the mishna? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who maintains that with regard to determining one’s obligation to bring an offering as a wealthy or destitute individual, the property that he uses for business is not taken into account. As we learned in a mishna:

notes.he: דאמר לקמן בפ' שום היתומים (ערכין דף כג:) גבי ערכין אם היה חמר נותן לו הכהן חמורו ואינו נוטלה להקדש:
notes.en: Whose is this? It is Rabbi Eliezer’s: who says below, in the chapter Shum HaYetomim (Arakhin 23b), regarding valuations: if he was a donkey driver, the priest leaves him his donkey and does not take it for the Temple treasury.

notes.he: דלא חשבינן ליה:
notes.en: Whose is this: that we do not count it?

messages.text: If he was a farmer, the treasurer gives him permission to keep his pair of oxen with which he plows the field. If he was a donkey driver, the treasurer gives him permission to keep his donkey.
messages.lead: When someone’s property is repossessed in order to pay his debt to the Temple treasury,

notes.he: צמד בקר דהיא פרנסתו:
notes.en: His pair: a pair of oxen, which is his livelihood.

notes.he: דאמר לקמן במקדיש נכסיו אם היה איכר [נותנין לו צמדו] אף הכא אם היה ספן נותן לו ספינתו:
notes.en: It is Rabbi Elazar’s [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s text; the daf reads Rabbi Eliezer]: who says below, regarding one who consecrates his property, that if he was a farmer [they leave him his pair]; so too here, if he was a sailor, he is left his ship.

messages.text: Mishna

The sum fixed by the Torah based on the years of age is in accordance with the age of the subject of the vow; how so? A youth who valuated an elder gives the valuation of an elder, and an elder who valuated a youth gives the valuation of a youth.

notes.he: מבן כ' ועד בן ששים דהוי ערכו נ' שקלים:
notes.en: Mishna. A youth: [one] from twenty to sixty years old, whose valuation is fifty shekels.

notes.he: [השנים בנידר שתולין זמן השנים בנידר ולא במדיר כדמפרש כיצד ילד שהעריך את הזקן כו':
notes.en: [The years follow the one vowed: they make the time of the years depend on the one vowed, not on the one who makes the vow, as it explains: How so? A youth who valuated an elder, etc.]

messages.text: And the distinction based on sex that is written in the halakhot of valuations is stated with regard to the one valuated; how so? A man who valuated a woman gives the valuation of a woman, and a woman who valuated a man gives the valuation of a man.

notes.he: ולא אזלינן בקצב הערך בתר מעריך:
notes.en: The valuations follow the one valuated: and in fixing the amount of the valuation we do not follow the one who valuates.

messages.text: And the different valuation based on the age of the one valuated is determined at the time one takes the vow of valuation; how so?

If one valuated another when he was less than five years old, when his valuation is five shekels, and before payment to the Temple treasury the subject of the vow became more than five years old, when his valuation is ten shekels; or if one valuated another when he was less than twenty years old, when his valuation is ten shekels, and before payment to the Temple treasury the subject of the vow became more than twenty years old, when his valuation is fifty shekels, in all these cases he gives payment according to the age of the subject of the valuation at the time of the valuation.

notes.dh: הערך בזמן הערך תולין את הערך בזמן שהעריך
notes.he: כיצד העריך פחות מבן חמש ולא הספיק ליתן הערך עד שנעשה יותר מבן חמש (אינו נותן אלא ערך כו'. ולא הספיק ליתן הערך עד שנעשה יותר על בן חמש) או פחות מעשרים כו' אינו נותן אלא כמה שהיה חייב ליתן בזמן שהעריך:
notes.en: The valuation at the time of the valuation: they make the valuation depend on the time he valuated. How so? He valuated [someone] less than five years old, and did not manage to give the valuation before he became more than five; or less than twenty, etc.: he gives only what he was obligated to give at the time he valuated.

messages.text: For a male, Leviticus 27:3–7 sets twenty shekels, not ten, from five to twenty years; ten is the figure for a female of that age.
Gemara
You have compared pledges of assessments for the Temple treasury, i.e., one who takes a vow to donate a certain person’s assessment, to vows of valuations.
messages.quote: And the valuation is determined at the time one takes the vow of valuation

notes.he: בפ"ק (לעיל ערכין דף ד:) דאמרינן נדר בערכך נפשות נדר היינו דמים בערכך היינו ערכין היקישן הכתוב להני תרי מילי:
notes.en: Gemara. You compared assessments to valuations: in the first chapter (above, 4b), where we say: “He vowed” with “by your valuation of persons”: “vowed” refers to assessments, “by your valuation” refers to valuations; the verse compared them for these two matters.

notes.he: אתה הקשית אותה דכתיב בבהמה טמאה דכתיב והעריך אותה הכהן ואין ערכין לבהמה אלא דמים דכתיב כערכך כן יקום אלא מ"ט מפיק ליה בלשון ערכין להקיש דמים לערכין לאלו הדינין דמרגלית לקלים כדאמר בפרק שום היתומים ונתן את הערכך ביום ההוא שלא ישהא]:
notes.en: You compared it: for it is written regarding an impure animal, “and the priest shall valuate it” (Leviticus 27:12), yet there is no valuation for an animal, only assessment, as it is written, “according to your valuation, so it shall stand.” Why, then, does it express it in the language of valuations? To compare assessments to valuations for these laws: a pearl for the light, as it says in the chapter Shum HaYetomim [on] “and he shall give your valuation on that day,” that he should not hold it back.

messages.text: This comparison applies with regard to a pearl belonging to light people, i.e., the poor. In other words, just as the assessment of a pearl is determined by the pearl’s location in a village of the poor rather than by the potential price of the pearl in the city market, so too, the valuation of a person is determined at the time of the valuation.

notes.he: דאזלינן במרגלית בתר קלים דכתיב בערכין ונתן את הערכך ביום ההוא ודרשינן לקמן (ערכין דף כד.) שלא ישהה מרגלית לקלים עני שהעריך עצמו ובא כהן להעריכו ויש לו מרגלית שוה ל' סלעים אין אומרים אם משהין אותה עד שיעלוה לכרך שיש שם עשיר והוא יקננה בנ' סלעים הילכך נ' סלעים יש לו ויתן ערך שלם אין אומרים כן ואין להקדש אלא מקומו ושעתו וה"נ בדמים אם אמר דמי מרגלית זו עלי אין שמין אותה לפי מכר הכרכים אלא לפי מכר אותה שעה ואותו מקום:
notes.en: A pearl for the light: for with a pearl we follow the light [the poor], as it is written regarding valuations, “and he shall give your valuation on that day” (Leviticus 27:23), and we expound below (24a) that a pearl is not held back for the light. A poor man valuated himself, and the priest came to valuate him, and he has a pearl worth thirty sela. We do not say: if it is kept until it is brought up to a city where there is a rich man who would buy it for fifty sela, then he has fifty sela and should give a full valuation. We do not say so; the Temple treasury has only its place and its time. So too with assessments: if one said, “The value of this pearl is upon me,” we do not assess it by the sale price in the cities, but by the price at that time and in that place.

notes.he: כלומר אדם קל עני שהקדיש נכסיו והיתה לו מרגלית משובחת אין שמין אותה כן אילו היתה ביד עשיר שיכול להמתין היתה שוה כך וכך או מי שהיה מעלה אותה לכרך פלוני היה מוכרה ביוקר אלא אין להקדש אלא כמה שהיא שוה במקומו של מקדיש ושעתו שאין ממתינין עד לשוק שתמכר ביוקר. [וכן פרה אין ממתינין אותה לאטליז אלא להכי איתקש דמים לערכין דאין לו אלא בזמן הערך:
notes.en: A pearl for the light: that is, a light, poor person who consecrated his property and had a fine pearl. We do not assess it at what it would be worth in the hands of a rich man who can wait, or at the high price for which one who brought it up to such-and-such a city would sell it; rather, the Temple treasury has only what it is worth in the place of the one consecrating and at his time, for we do not wait for market day for it to be sold at a high price. [And likewise a cow is not held for the butchers’ market.] So for this assessments were compared to valuations: that it has only [its value] at the time of the valuation.

messages.text: And similarly, the comparison teaches that the court is required to assess the value of the limb by its significance, i.e., in the case of a limb that is vital to one’s survival, the valuation of the limb is equivalent to the valuation of the whole person.

notes.he: שאם העריך דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו כגון שאמר ערך ראשי עלי נותן ערך שלם דכתיב גבי ערכין בערכך נפשות דבתר נפש אזלינן:
notes.en: And to assess it by its significance: that if he valuated something on which life depends, for instance he said, “The valuation of my head is upon me,” he gives a full valuation, as it is written regarding valuations, “by your valuation of persons,” so we follow the person [as a whole].

notes.he: שאם אמר דמי ראשי או כבדי עלי נידון בכבודו של אבר כמו בערכין ונותן דמי כולו מפני שהנשמה תלויה בו]:
notes.en: And to assess it by its significance: that if he said, “The value of my head,” or “of my liver, is upon me,” it is assessed by the significance of the limb, as with valuations, and he gives the value of all of him, because life depends on it.

messages.text: One might have thought that we should compare valuations to assessments in that the one pledging must give a person’s valuation not corresponding to his value at the time of the pledge but in accordance with his value at the time of giving, as is the case with regard to vows of assessments.

notes.he: דבדמים פשיטא לן דיהיב כשעת נתינה ולא כשעת נדר דהא כעבד בשוק שמין אותו ואם אמר דמי עלי בתשרי ובניסן בא לב"ד מי יודע מה היה שוה בשעת נדר ושעת נתינה היינו שעה שהוא בא לב"ד:
notes.en: That he gives according to the time of giving: for with assessments it is obvious to us that he gives according to the time of giving and not the time of the vow, since he is assessed like a slave in the market. If he said, “My value is upon me,” in Tishrei, and came to court in Nisan, who knows what he was worth at the time of the vow? And the time of giving is the time he comes to court.

notes.he: פי' רש"י דבדמים פשיטא ליה דיהיב כשעת נתינה ולא כשעת הנדר דהא כעבד בשוק שמין אותו ואם אמר דמי עלי בתשרי ובניסן בא לב"ד מי יודע מה היה שוה בשעת הנדר ושעת נתינה היינו [שעה] שהוא בא לב"ד לשון רש"י ותימה מאי סברא הוא זה דלמה יש לנו לומר שהיה שוה יותר מעכשיו ואם אנו רואים שהוא חלש עכשיו ואז היה גבור אז ידענו בודאי שהיה שוה יותר ונפסיד ההקדש מאחר שאנו רואים שהיה שוה יותר סלע לכל הפחות לכך אור"י דאין זו סברא אלא שום ראיה מקרא יש בו ועוד דתנן לקמן פרק האומר משקלי (ערכין דף כ. ושם) מת הנידר לא יתנו היורשים לפי שאין דמים למתים ואם היה הטעם מסברא דאזלינן בתר נתינה התם לא שייך למימר הך סברא שהרי ידענו שהיה שוה בחייו סלע לכל הפחות וא"כ מפני מה אנו פוטרים היורשים מכל וכל אלא ודאי שום קרא יש בו:
notes.en: That he gives according to the time of giving: Rashi explained that with assessments it is obvious to the Gemara that he gives according to the time of giving and not the time of the vow, since he is assessed like a slave in the market; and if he said, “My value is upon me,” in Tishrei and came to court in Nisan, who knows what he was worth at the time of the vow? And the time of giving is the time he comes to court. So far Rashi’s words. This is puzzling: what reasoning is this? Why should we say he was worth more than now? And if we see that he is weak now and was strong then, we certainly know he was worth more then, and we would be causing the Temple treasury a loss, since we see he was worth at least a sela more. Therefore Ri says this is not a matter of reasoning; rather there is some proof from a verse for it. Furthermore, we learned below, in the chapter HaOmer Mishkali (Arakhin 20a): if the one whose value was vowed died, the heirs do not give, because the dead have no value. If the reason were from reasoning, that we follow the time of giving, that reasoning would not apply there, for we know he was worth at least a sela while alive; so why do we exempt the heirs entirely? Rather, there is certainly some verse for it.

notes.he: שיתן כשעת נתינה כדכתיב ונתן את ערכך ביום ההוא. והאי ערכך היינו דמים כדאמרן לעיל:
notes.en: One might have thought we should compare valuations to assessments: that he gives according to the time of giving, as it is written, “and he shall give your valuation on that day” (Leviticus 27:23); and this “your valuation” means assessments, as we said above.

messages.text: To counter this suggestion the verse states: “According to your valuation it shall stand”, which teaches that the one making the valuation gives his donation only according to the valuation of the person at the time of the valuation, as stated in the mishna.

verse.he: אִם־מִשְּׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ כְּעֶרְכְּךָ יָקוּם׃
verse.en: If the land is consecrated as of the jubilee year, its assessment stands.

notes.he: דמשמע ערכין בשעת ערך שאם העריך עצמו בן ששים ונעשה יותר על ששים נותן ערך גדול ולא ערך זקן:
notes.en: The verse states “according to your valuation it shall stand”: which implies valuations by the time of the valuation; so that if he valuated himself at sixty and became more than sixty, he gives the large valuation and not the valuation of an elder.

notes.he: כשעת הערך יקום:
notes.en: The verse states “according to your valuation, so it shall stand”: it stands as at the time of the valuation.

messages.text: Mishna

The Torah provides three age categories that determine the amount of the valuation: From the age of one month until age five, from age five until age twenty, and from age twenty until age sixty. For anyone less than one month old there is no valuation.

The halakhic status of the thirtieth day is like that of the period preceding thirty days, and therefore the one who took the vow is exempt. Likewise, the halakhic status of the fifth year and the twentieth year is like that of the period preceding them.

notes.he: ואם אמר ערך פלוני קטן עלי ואותו קטן היה באותו יום בן ל' הוי כלמטה ולא אמר כלום ואין ערך לפחות מבן חדש דהכי כתיב ואם מבן חדש וגו':
notes.en: Mishna. The thirtieth day is like below it: if he said, “The valuation of this little one is upon me,” and that little one was thirty days old that day, it is like below, and he has said nothing; for there is no valuation for one less than a month old, as it is written, “And if from a month old…” (Leviticus 27:6).

notes.he: שאם העריך ביום שלשים כאילו העריך פחות מבן חדש ואינו נותן כלום:
notes.en: [The thirtieth day is like below it: if he valuated on the thirtieth day, it is as if he valuated one less than a month old, and he gives nothing.]

messages.text: As it is stated: “And if it is from sixty years old and upward”, and we derive all the other age categories from the sixtieth year: Just as the halakhic status of the sixtieth year, where upward is written, is like that of the period preceding it, so too, the halakhic status of the fifth year and the twentieth year is like that of the period preceding them.

verse.he: וְאִם מִבֶּן־שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה אִם־זָכָר וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שָׁקֶל וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֲשָׂרָה שְׁקָלִים׃
verse.en: If the age is sixty years or over, the equivalent is fifteen shekels in the case of a male and ten shekels for a female.

notes.he: משמע ששלמה שנת ששים ואז הוא נידון כזקן אבל בשנת ששים נידון כילד:
notes.en: And upward: implies that the sixtieth year has been completed, and then he is judged as an elder; but in the sixtieth year he is judged as a youth.

notes.dh: שנת חמש ושנת עשרים כלמטה הימנה
notes.he: שאם העריך בשנת חמש נותן ערך בן שלשים כאילו בשלש או בארבע שנה העריך כדכתיב ואם מבן חדש ועד בן חמש שנה וכן שנת עשרים כלמטה הימנה שנותן ערך בן חמש שנאמר] ואם מבן ששים שנה ומעלה דכיון דכתיב בן ששים ואיצטריך למיכתב ומעלה ש"מ דמה שיעריך מבן ששים ואילך הוי כלמעלה הא שנת ששים גופה כלמטה הימנה:
notes.en: The fifth year and the twentieth year are like below them: if he valuated in the fifth year, he gives the valuation of one from thirty days [the first bracket], as if he had valuated in the third or fourth year, as it is written, “And if from a month old until five years old.” And so the twentieth year is like below it, so that he gives the valuation of one from five years. As it is stated, “And if from sixty years old and upward”: since it is written “sixty years old” and it needed to write “and upward,” learn from it that what one valuates from sixty onward is like above, but the sixtieth year itself is like below it.

messages.text: Is that so? Can one derive a halakha in this manner? If the Torah rendered the halakhic status of the sixtieth year like that of the period preceding it in order to be stringent and require one who valuated a sixty-year-old person to pay his valuation to the Temple treasury, shall we render the halakhic status of the fifth year and the twentieth year like that of the period preceding them in order to be lenient and pay a lower sum?

notes.he: בתמיה. כלומר וכי כן הוא אם עשינו שנת ששים כלמטה להחמיר דערך גדול יש לו לפחות מבן ששים נ' סלעים וליותר על בן ששים אין ערך אלא ט"ו סלעים:
notes.en: Is that so? If we made: said as a question. That is: is it so? If we made the sixtieth year like below, that is to be stringent, for one younger than sixty has a large valuation of fifty sela, and one older than sixty has a valuation of only fifteen sela.

notes.dh: [והרי אנו למידין לכולם משנת ששים כו'
notes.he: הין אם עושה שנת ששים כלמטה היינו להחמיר שמעשרים ועד ששים ערכין נ' שקל ומס' ומעלה אינו אלא ט"ו שקל. נעשה שנת חמש ושנת עשרים כלמטה הימנה להקל שפחות מחמש אין ערכו גדול כשל חמש וכן פחות מכ' ערכו ממועט משל למעלה מעשרים]:
notes.en: [And we learn them all from the sixtieth year, etc. Is that so? If he makes the sixtieth year like below, that is to be stringent, for from twenty to sixty the valuation is fifty shekels and from sixty upward it is only fifteen shekels. Shall we make the fifth year and the twentieth year like below to be lenient? For below five the valuation is not as great as that of five, and likewise below twenty the valuation is smaller than above twenty.]

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states “year” with regard to the fifth and twentieth years (see Leviticus 27:3–6), and “year” with regard to the sixtieth year (Leviticus 27:7), for a verbal analogy.

notes.he: נאמר בששים שנה [ונאמר] בחמש ובעשרים שנה לג"ש כלומר היקישא הוא ואין משיבין על היקישא בין להקל בין להחמיר:
notes.en: The verse states “year,” “year”: “year” is stated with sixty, [and] “year” with five and with twenty, for a verbal analogy; that is, it is a comparison [set by the verse], and one does not refute such a comparison, whether to be lenient or to be stringent.

messages.text: Just as the halakhic status of the year stated with regard to the sixtieth year is like that of the period preceding it, so too, the halakhic status of the year stated with regard to the fifth year and the twentieth year is like that of the period preceding them, both in order to be lenient and in order to be stringent.

notes.he: דערך [יותר] על בן כ' יותר גדול הוא מפחות מבן עשרים וכן בבן חמש כדכתיב בקראי:
notes.en: To be lenient: for the valuation of one [older] than twenty is larger than that of one younger than twenty, and so too with five, as written in the verses.

messages.text: Their halakhic status remains like that of the period preceding it, until they will be aged one month and one day beyond the fifth, twentieth, and sixtieth years.

notes.he: לעולם שנת חמש ושנת עשרים ושנת ששים כלמטה עד שתשלם כל השנה וחדש ויום א' משנה האחרת:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: the fifth year, the twentieth year and the sixtieth year are always like below, until the whole year is complete and a month and one day of the next year [have passed].

notes.dh: [ר' אלעזר אומר עד שיהו יתירות על השנים חודש ויום אחד
notes.he: שלעולם אינו נותן ערך בן חמש עד שיהא בן חמש ויותר על החמש חודש ויום אחד. וכן נמי לעולם אינו נותן ערך בן עשרים עד שיהא בן עשרים וחדש ויום אחד]:
notes.en: [Rabbi Eliezer says: until they are a month and one day beyond the years: so that he never gives the valuation of one five years old until he is five and a month and one day beyond five; and likewise he never gives the valuation of one twenty years old until he is twenty and a month and one day.]

messages.caption: The thirtieth day and the fifth, twentieth and sixtieth years count with the years below them: a stringency at sixty, a leniency at five and twenty.

messages.text: Gemara

Evidently, the verbal analogy in the mishna is free, i.e., in each verse the word “year” is superfluous, and therefore can be used in the verbal analogy. This means that the halakha derived from the verbal analogy is considered as though it is written explicitly in the Torah.
messages.quote: the verse states “year” … and “year” … for a verbal analogy

notes.he: האי שנה שנה דאין צריך לגופו אלא לידון בג"ש דאל"כ איכא למיפרך כדפרכינן במתני' הין אם עשה שנת ששים כלמטה כו':
notes.en: Free: this “year,” “year” is not needed for itself but to be used for the verbal analogy; for otherwise it could be refuted as we refuted in the mishna: “Is that so? If he made the sixtieth year like below,” etc.

messages.text: The significance of this fact is that if a verbal analogy is not free, it can be refuted by logical reasoning. In this case the refutation would be as we refuted it in the mishna, that if the fifth year and the twentieth year are considered the same as the respective periods preceding them, this generates a leniency.

notes.he: במתניתין:
notes.en: Gemara. It could be refuted as we refuted it: in the mishna.

messages.text: The verbal analogy is free, as both the first written mention of “year” and the second written mention of “year” are superfluous.

notes.he: דמצי למכתב ואם מבן ה' שנים ועד בן כ' ואנא ידענא דעשרים נמי (כ') בשנים משתעי שנה ל"ל ובן ששים:
notes.en: The words “year” are superfluous: for it could have written, “And if from five years old until twenty,” and I would know that “twenty” too speaks of years. Why do I need “year”? And so with “sixty.”

notes.he: [שנה שנה יתירי כתיב כלומר למה] לי למיכתב שנה בשנת עשרים ושנת (עשרים) [ששים] ליגמר מבן חמש שנים אלא להקיש:
notes.en: [The words “year,” “year” are written superfluously; that is, why] do I need it to write “year” with the twentieth year and with the [sixtieth] year? Let it be learned from “five years old”! Rather, it is for the comparison.

notes.he: ואי' דמפרשי שנה שנה יתירא דמצי למימר ואם מבן חמש שנים עד בן כ' ולא איצטריך למיכתב שנים בתרא וכל כולה שנה בתראי:
notes.en: And some explain [that the superfluous] “year” (and so Rashi explained, in the comment beginning “the words ‘year’ are superfluous”) is the extra “years,” for it could have said, “And if from five years old until twenty,” and would not have needed to write the latter “years”; and all of them are the latter “year.” [The text of this note is partly garbled.]

messages.text: Let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, as, if it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, doesn’t he say that the word “until” means until and including?

notes.he: דמצריך קרא למילף שנת עשרים כלמטה דלא כרבי דאי כרבי האמר עד ועד בכלל וכיון דכתיב מבן חמש שנים ועד בן עשרים ממילא ידענא דשנת עשרים בכלל והיינו כלמטה:
notes.en: Let us say the mishna: which needs a verse to teach that the twentieth year is like below, is not in accordance with Rabbi. For if it were Rabbi’s, he says “until” means until and including; and since it is written, “from five years old until twenty,” I would know on my own that the twentieth year is included, which is “like below.”

notes.he: דאי ר' היא הא אמר לקמן עד ועד בכלל כלומר כיון דכתב עד בן חמש שנים ועד בן עשרים שנה ממילא שמעינן דכלמטה הימנה דעד ועד בכלל ולא צריכא ג"ש:
notes.en: For if it were Rabbi’s, he says below that “until” means until and including; that is, since it wrote “until five years old” and “until twenty years old,” we would understand on our own that it is like below it, for “until” means until and including, and the verbal analogy would not be needed.

messages.text: With regard to valuations, the Torah states: “From twenty years old until sixty years old…And if it is from five years old until twenty years old…And if it is from one month old until five years old” (Leviticus 27:3–6). Accordingly, in the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi there should be no need for a verbal analogy to include the fifth year and the twentieth year in the periods preceding them.

The verse states: “For whoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day”. One might have thought that the prohibition against eating leaven applies from the first day and onward but the first day is not included, and likewise that the prohibition continues until the seventh day but the seventh day is not included.
messages.lead: The Gemara provides the source of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi’s opinion. As it is taught in a baraita concerning the festival of Passover:

verse.he: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים מַצּוֹת תֹּאכֵלוּ אַךְ בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן תַּשְׁבִּיתוּ שְּׂאֹר מִבָּתֵּיכֶם כִּי ׀ כׇּל־אֹכֵל חָמֵץ וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מִיּוֹם הָרִאשֹׁן עַד־יוֹם הַשְּׁבִעִי׃
verse.en: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; on the very first day you shall remove leaven from your houses, for whoever eats leavened bread from the first day to the seventh day, that person shall be cut off from Israel.

notes.he: מיום הראשון ואילך יהא מוזהר על חמץ ולא ראשון בכלל:
notes.en: One might have thought: that from the first day onward he is warned against leaven, and the first is not included.

notes.dh: יכול ראשון ולא ראשון בכלל שביעי ולא שביעי בכלל
notes.he: וא"ת היאך אפשר לומר כן והכתיב (שמות י״ג:ו׳) שבעת ימים תאכל מצות וי"ל דלחיוב כרת קאמר דכרת בהאי קרא כתיב דכתיב כי כל אוכל מחמצת ונכרתה מיום הראשון עד יום השביעי מש"ה מייתי ת"ל עד יום האחד ועשרים בערב והאי קרא כרת נמי כתיב ביה:
notes.en: One might have thought: the first but not including the first, the seventh but not including the seventh: And if you ask, how is it possible to say so? Isn’t it written, “Seven days you shall eat matzot” (Exodus 13:6)? One can answer that it speaks of liability to karet, for karet is written in this verse, as it is written, “For whoever eats leavened bread, that soul shall be cut off … from the first day until the seventh day” (Exodus 12:15). That is why it cites, “The verse states: until the twenty-first day in the evening,” and karet is also written with that verse.

messages.text: This is similar to the matter that is stated with regard to a leper: “And the leprosy covers all the skin of him who has the mark from his head to his feet, as far as the priest can see…it is all turned white: He is pure”. This verse is understood as follows: The mark reaches from his head, but his head is not included; it reaches to his feet, but his feet are not included.

verse.he: וְאִם־פָּרוֹחַ תִּפְרַח הַצָּרַעַת בָּעוֹר וְכִסְּתָה הַצָּרַעַת אֵת כׇּל־עוֹר הַנֶּגַע מֵרֹאשׁוֹ וְעַד־רַגְלָיו לְכׇל־מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן׃ וְרָאָה הַכֹּהֵן וְהִנֵּה כִסְּתָה הַצָּרַעַת אֶת־כׇּל־בְּשָׂרוֹ וְטִהַר אֶת־הַנָּגַע כֻּלּוֹ הָפַךְ לָבָן טָהוֹר הוּא׃
verse.en: If the eruption spreads out over the skin so that it covers all the skin of the affected person from head to foot, wherever the priest can see— if the priest sees that the eruption has covered the whole body—he shall pronounce as pure the affected person, who is pure from having turned all white.

notes.he: דפשיטא לן כדמפרש לקמן מראשו ולא ראשו בכלל:
notes.en: Like the matter that is stated, “from his head to his feet”: which is obvious to us, as is explained below: “from his head” and not including his head.

notes.he: ראשו ולא ראשו בכלל עד רגלו ולא רגלו בכלל משום דכתיב לכל מראה עיני הכהן וראשו ורגליו אינן נסקרין ביחד בסקירה אחת:
notes.en: His head and not including his head, until his feet and not including his feet: because it is written, “as far as the priest can see” (Leviticus 13:12), and his head and his feet are not examined together in a single look.

messages.text: Therefore, one might have thought the prohibition against consuming leaven on the festival of Passover likewise does not apply to the endpoints mentioned in the verse.
Therefore, the verse states: “You shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening”. This proves that the seventh day of the Festival is included.

verse.he: בָּרִאשֹׁן בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ בָּעֶרֶב תֹּאכְלוּ מַצֹּת עַד יוֹם הָאֶחָד וְעֶשְׂרִים לַחֹדֶשׁ בָּעָרֶב׃
verse.en: In the first month, from the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread until the twenty-first day of the month at evening.

notes.dh: ת"ל עד יום האחד ועשרים לחדש בערב
notes.he: אלמא יום ראשון בכלל כדכתיב ברישא דקרא בערב תאכלו מצות ושביעי נמי בכלל מסיפיה דקרא כדכתיב בערב:
notes.en: The verse states, “until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening”: so the first day is included, as written at the beginning of the verse, “in the evening you shall eat matzot,” and the seventh is also included, from the end of the verse, as it is written, “in the evening.”

notes.dh: ת"ל עד יום האחד ועשרים לחדש בערב
notes.he: לסוף הימים היינו ראשון ושביעי בכלל:
notes.en: The verse states, “until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening”: at the end of the days, meaning that the first and the seventh are included.

messages.text: It is not necessary to cite this verse, as the prohibition against consuming leaven is from the first day of Passover, and the first day is included; and the ban continues until the seventh day, and the seventh day is included.

notes.he: אלא כיון דכתיב ביה מיום הראשון ועד יום השביעי תרווייהו הוו בכלל ולא איצטריך ג"ש:
notes.en: Rabbi says: It is not necessary: rather, since it is written, “from the first day until the seventh day,” both are included, and no verbal analogy is needed.

messages.text: Accordingly, with regard to valuations, even without a verbal analogy Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi should maintain that the twentieth year is included in the preceding period.
You may even say that the opinion in the mishna is in accordance with that of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, as the verses offset each other, and therefore their meaning is unclear without the verbal analogy.
messages.quote: Let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi

notes.he: שקולין הן המדרשות. לפי מדרשו של רבי יש להכריען כלמטה ויש להכריען כלמעלה כדכתיב מבן חדש ועד בן חמש שנים והיה ערכך וגו' ואמרינן עד ועד בכלל הרי בן חמש כלמטה והדר כתיב ואם מבן חמש שנים ועד בן כ' וגו' ולרבי מבן חמש ובן חמש בכלל דהאמר מיום הראשון הראשון בכלל הרי שנת ה' כלמעלה הלכך אי לאו ג"ש לא קמה לן הכרעה להיכא:
notes.en: The verses offset each other: the expositions are evenly balanced. By Rabbi’s exposition, one could decide [the fifth year] as like below and one could decide it as like above. For it is written, “from a month old until five years old, then your valuation…,” and we say “until” is until and including, so five is like below. Then it is written, “And if from five years old until twenty…,” and according to Rabbi, “from five” includes five, since he says that “from the first day” means the first is included; so the fifth year is like above. Therefore, without the verbal analogy we would have no decision either way.

notes.he: שאין אנו יודעין אם נאמר עד ועד בכלל אי לא דכשם דמשמע למטה כך משמע למעלה. כיצד שאם נאמר אם מבן חדש ועד בן חמש שנים דמשמע שתהא שנת חמש בכלל הכי נמי כתיב אם מבן חמש שנים ועד בן עשרים שנה דמשמע שתהא שנת חמש כלמעלה הימנה עד עשרים הילכך איצטריך ג"ש:
notes.en: The verses offset each other: for we do not know whether to say “until” is until and including or not; for just as it implies below, so it implies above. How so? If we say, “And if from a month old until five years old,” it implies that the fifth year is included [in that bracket]; but it is also written, “And if from five years old until twenty years old,” which implies that the fifth year is like above it, up to twenty. Therefore a verbal analogy is needed.

messages.text: Since it is written: “From one month old until five years old” (Leviticus 27:6), this ostensibly includes the fifth year within the stated category. If so, why do I need this mention of five years as well: “And if it is from five years old until twenty years old, then your valuation shall be for the male twenty shekels” (Leviticus 27:5)?

notes.he: הכי ה"ל למיכתב ועד בן עשרים שנה והיה ערכך וגו' ועד בן ששים שנה והיה ערכך וגו':
notes.en: Why do I need “from five” as well: it should have written thus: “and until twenty years old, then your valuation…,” and “until sixty years old, then your valuation….”

messages.text: Therefore, with regard to the fifth year, as both verses mention that year, the verses offset each other. Consequently, even according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi the verbal analogy is necessary.
The mark reaches from his head, but his head is not included; it reaches to his feet, but his feet are not included. From where do we derive this interpretation?
messages.lead: The Master said above, with regard to a leper:
messages.quote: his head, but his head is not included; … his feet, but his feet are not included

messages.text: If you wish, say that it is deduced logically: The signs of leprosy of his body are different from the signs of leprosy of his head with regard to the different colors of hair that indicate leprosy.

notes.he: דסימני נגע שבמקום שיער נידון בשיער צהוב ובנגע שבמקום בשר נידון בשיער לבן ובפסיון:
notes.en: The signs of his body are different from the signs of his head: for the signs of a mark in a place of hair [the head] are judged by yellow hair, and of a mark in a place of flesh by white hair and by spreading.

notes.dh: משום הכי לא אמרינן ראשו בכלל ורגליו בכלל דשאני סימנים דגופו מסימנים דראשו
notes.he: דסימנין דגופו נידונין בשער לבן ובפסיון וסימנים דראשו נידונין בשיער צהוב]:
notes.en: That is why we do not say his head is included and his feet are included: for the signs of his body are different from the signs of his head. The signs of his body are judged by white hair and by spreading, and the signs of his head are judged by yellow hair.

messages.text: Alternatively, if you wish, say instead that it is derived from the phrase in that verse: “As far as the priest can see.” This excludes a leprous mark on the head, which is obscured from the priest’s view by the hair, as well as leprous marks between the toes.

notes.he: ואינו יכול לראות בראש מפני השיער וברגל בין אצבע לאצבע:
notes.en: As far as the priest can see: and he cannot see on the head because of the hair, nor on the foot between toe and toe.

notes.dh: ואי בעית אימא לכל מראה עיני הכהן
notes.he: ואינו יכול לראות בראש מפני השער וברגל בין אצבע לאצבע וא"ת הכא משמע דפרח בכולו לא שייך ברגל ובאיזהו מקומן (זבחים דף מט:) לא משמע כך דאיכא התם ר' נתן בן אבטולמוס אמר מנין לפריחה בבגדים שהיא טהורה נאמר קרחת וגבחת בבגדים ונאמר קרחת וגבחת באדם מה להלן פרחה בכולו טהור אף כאן פרחה בכולו טהור והתם מנלן דכתיב מראשו ועד רגליו מה להלן כולו הפך טהור פירוש ברגל אף כאן פי' בראשו כולו הפך טהור [משמע] דפריחה שייך שפיר ברגל דיליף ראש מרגל:
notes.en: Alternatively, say: “As far as the priest can see”: he cannot see on the head because of the hair, nor on the foot between toe and toe. And if you ask: here it implies that [the rule of a mark that] spread over all of him does not apply to the foot, yet in Eizehu Mekoman (Zevaḥim 49b) it does not imply so. For there Rabbi Natan ben Avtolemos says: From where is it derived that [a mark that] spread over all of a garment is pure? “Baldness of the back” and “baldness of the front” are stated with garments, and “baldness of the back” and “baldness of the front” are stated with a person; just as there, if it spread over all of him he is pure, so too here, if it spread over all of it, it is pure. And there, from where do we derive it? For it is written, “from his head to his feet”: just as there, [at] his foot, if all of it turned [white] he is pure, so too here, [at] his head, if all of it turned [white] he is pure. [This implies] that spreading does apply to the foot, since it derives the head from the foot.

notes.he: ואין עיני הכהן שולטות להסתכל בראיה אחת ראשו ורגליו:
notes.en: As far as the priest can see: and the priest’s eyes cannot take in his head and his feet in one look.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that Rabbi Eliezer says: Their halakhic status remains like that of the period preceding it, until they will be aged one month and one day beyond the respective years. With regard to this opinion, it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: until they will be aged one month and one day beyond the … years

messages.text: It is stated here, with regard to valuations, “upward” (Leviticus 27:7), and it is stated there, with regard to the census of the Levites in the wilderness: “From one month old and upward you shall number them”. Just as there, in the case of the census, the verse means: From one month and one day old, so too here, with regard to valuations, the verse means that each respective category is counted from one month and one day old beyond the stated ages of five years, twenty years, or sixty years.

verse.he: פְּקֹד אֶת־בְּנֵי לֵוִי לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם כׇּל־זָכָר מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ וָמַעְלָה תִּפְקְדֵם׃
verse.en: Record the descendants of Levi by ancestral house and by clan; record every male among them from the age of one month up.

notes.he: גבי לוים חדש ומעלה מה להלן חדש ויום אחד כדכתיב מבן חדש ומעלה דכבר נכנס בה חדש האחר אף כאן חדש ויום אחד:
notes.en: And it is stated there: regarding the Levites, “a month old and upward.” Just as there it means a month and one day, as it is written, “from a month old and upward,” meaning he has already entered the next month, so too here, a month and one day.

notes.he: וחפשנו אחר מקרא זה ולא מצאנוהו כ"א ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה ושמא דריש הכי מדכתיב ופדויו מבן חדש דמשמע מבן חדש ומעלה מדלא כתיב בן חדש:
notes.en: “And his redeemed, from a month old and upward” [so Tosafot’s text of the Gemara]: We searched for this verse and did not find it, only “and his redeemed, from a month old shall you redeem” (Numbers 18:16). Perhaps it expounds this from what is written, “and his redeemed, from a month old,” which implies from a month old and upward, since it did not write “a month old.”

notes.he: חדש ויום אחד דכתיב ביה ומעלה:
notes.en: Just as there: a month and one day, for “and upward” is written there.

messages.text: And why doesn’t Rabbi Eliezer say that the verse dealing with valuation should be understood like the verse written there, with regard to the census, in the following manner: Just as there it is one day more than the enumerated age of thirty days, so too here, it should be one day more than the enumerated ages of five years, twenty years, and sixty years. Why does Rabbi Eliezer add a month?

notes.he: מה מעלה דכתיב גבי חדש לא הוי אלא חד יומא אף מעלה דהכא גבי שנים לא הוי אלא חד יומא:
notes.en: Just as there it is one day: just as “upward” written with “a month” is only one day, so too “upward” here, with years, is only one day.

notes.he: יותר על מה שכתוב בתורה דכתיב ופדוייו מבן חדש תפדה אף הכא נמי חד יומא שלא יהו יתירות על השנים אלא יום אחד:
notes.en: Just as there it is one day: more than what is written in the Torah, as it is written, “and his redeemed, from a month old shall you redeem” (Numbers 18:16); so too here, one day, so that they are only one day beyond the years.

messages.text: If so, that only one day should be added, what purpose does this verbal analogy from the census serve? Even without any connection to the verse dealing with the census, it would be understood in the case of valuations that the new period begins from the day after the respective year is fully completed.

notes.he: בלא ג"ש ידענא דחד יומא בעינן דהא ומעלה כתיב:
notes.en: What purpose does the verbal analogy serve: without the verbal analogy I would know that we require one day, since “and upward” is written.

notes.he: אלא להכי אתיא ג"ש לחדש ויום אחד:
notes.en: [If so, what purpose does the verbal analogy serve? Rather, the verbal analogy comes for this: a month and one day.]

messages.text: With regard to the period of one year stated with regard to sacrificial animals, e.g., “sheep in their first year” (Numbers 28:3); and the one year stated with regard to houses of walled cities, during which time it is permitted to redeem a sold house in a walled city (Leviticus 25:29); and the two years stated with regard to an ancestral field, during which one may not yet redeem an ancestral field he has sold (Leviticus 25:15); and the six years stated with regard to a Hebrew slave (Exodus 21:2); and similarly, the years stated with regard to a son and with regard to a daughter, as explained below;

notes.he: כגון (במדבר כ״ח:ג׳) כבשים בני שנה:
notes.en: A year stated with regard to consecrated animals: for example, “lambs in their first year” (Numbers 28:3).

notes.he: (שהוא) שהמוכר שדה אחוזה אינו רשאי לגאול עד שתהא ב' שנים ביד הלוקח דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:ט״ו-ט״ז) במספר שני תבואות ימכר לך ומיעוט שנים שתים:
notes.en: Two years of an ancestral field: one who sells an ancestral field may not redeem it until it has been two years in the buyer’s hands, as it is written, “according to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you” (Leviticus 25:15–16), and the minimum of “years” is two.

messages.text: all of these are calculated from the time of day at the start of the period to the time of day at the end of the period, i.e., these periods are units of whole years; they do not expire on predetermined dates, such as at the end of the calendar year.

notes.he: [י"ב חדש] מיום ליום. ולא [שנה] למניינו של עולם דאי למנין העולם מתשרי ועד ניסן עלתה לו שנה:
notes.en: [All of them] from time to time: [twelve months] from day to day, and not [a year] by the world’s count; for by the world’s count, from Tishrei until Nisan would already count for him as a year.

messages.text: With regard to the one year stated with regard to sacrificial animals, from where do we derive that it is calculated by whole years rather than calendar years?
messages.quote: year stated with regard to sacrificial animals

messages.text: The verse states: “A sheep in its first year”. Since the verse does not state: A sheep in the first year, it means a year based on the calculation of its own life, and not a year based on the counting of the world, i.e., the calendar year.

verse.he: וּבִמְלֹאת ׀ יְמֵי טׇהֳרָהּ לְבֵן אוֹ לְבַת תָּבִיא כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן־שְׁנָתוֹ לְעֹלָה וּבֶן־יוֹנָה אוֹ־תֹר לְחַטָּאת אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל־מוֹעֵד אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en: On the completion of her period of purification, for either son or daughter, she shall bring to the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, a lamb in its first year for a burnt offering, and a pigeon or a turtledove for a purgation offering.

notes.dh: שנתו שלו ולא שנתו של עולם
notes.he: הק' הרב שמואל בן הרב אלחנן ל"ל קרא תיפוק ליה מסברא דאלת"ה היאך נמצא תמידין כשרין לר"ה שאם נולד קודם ר"ה מיד כשנכנס ר"ה בן ב' שנים הוא ואנו כבש בן שנה בעינן לתמידין ואם הוא נולד יום ר"ה מחוסר זמן הוא ויש מפרשים דאין אנו מתחילין מנין שנתו כי אם מיום הרצאה כדאמרינן גבי בכור לפני ה' תאכלנו שנה בשנה ואמרינן (ר"ה דף ו:) דאין אנו מונין אלא מיום הרצאה ה"נ אמרינן הכא ואינו כן דלא אמרינן דין זה כ"א לענין בל תאחר אבל לענין מניין שניו לא דהא אמרינן בפ"ב דזבחים (דף כה:) דשעות פוסלות בקדשים פי' אם שחט כבש [ביום] השלמת שנתו קודם שהגיע מעת לעת דלידתו ולא הספיק לזרוק הדם עד שעבר מעת לעת לשעת לידתו פסול ואי אזלינן ביה אחר הרצאה לא תמצא דין זה שהרי לעולם הוא בן שנתו אלא ש"מ דאזלינן אחר הלידה ממש א"כ הדרא קושיא לדוכתיה ואומר מורי ה"ר שמואל דשפיר (איצטרכו תרי קראי) דאי לאו הכי לא אמרינן ביה מעת לעת כדאי' לקמן בפרק בתרא (ערכין דף לא.):
notes.en: In brief: “Its own year, and not the year of the world.” Rabbi Shmuel ben Rabbi Elḥanan asked: why is a verse needed? It follows from reasoning: otherwise, how could lambs for the daily offering ever be fit on Rosh HaShana? One born before Rosh HaShana would be in its second year as soon as Rosh HaShana came, while the daily offering requires a lamb in its first year; and one born on Rosh HaShana is too young to be offered. Some answer that an animal’s year is counted only from the day it becomes fit to be accepted, as is said of the firstborn, “year by year” (Rosh HaShana 6b), and so too here. Tosafot rejects this: that count applies only to the prohibition of delaying, not to counting an animal’s age, since Zevaḥim 25b rules that hours disqualify consecrated animals (a lamb slaughtered on the day its year ends, before the hour of its birth, whose blood was sprinkled only after that hour, is disqualified), which could never happen if we counted from fitness; so we count from the actual birth, and the question returns. [The author’s] teacher, Rabbi Shmuel, answers that the verse is still needed, for without it we would not count from time to time [to the hour] here, as stated in the last chapter (Arakhin 31a). Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: The halakha that the one year stated with regard to houses of walled cities is calculated by a whole year and not a calendar year is derived from the fact that it is written: “Then he may redeem it within a whole year after it is sold, for a full year he shall have the right of redemption”. The verse is referring to a year counted from the day of its own sale, and not the year of the counting of the world.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִמְכֹּר בֵּית־מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ עַד־תֹּם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ יָמִים תִּהְיֶה גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who sells a dwelling house in a walled city: It may be redeemed until a year has elapsed since its sale; the redemption period shall be a year.

messages.text: Concerning the two years stated with regard to an ancestral field, this is derived from the fact that it is written: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you”. The plural form of both “years” and “crops” indicates that the number of years does not necessarily correspond to the quantity of crops. Consequently, there are times when a person might eat three yields of crops in two years.

verse.he: בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה מֵאֵת עֲמִיתֶךָ בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי־תְבוּאֹת יִמְכׇּר־לָךְ׃
verse.en: In buying from your neighbor, you shall deduct only for the number of years since the jubilee; and in selling to you, you shall be charged only for the remaining crop years:

notes.he: כיון דכתיב שני שני תבואות במשמע תבואות ל"ל אלא מלמד שכל תבואה שימצא באותן ב' שנים יאכל ואפי' ג' כגון אם מכרו לו בניסן מליאה קמה ולא יגאלנה עד שתי שנים בניסן באותו יום ואם קדם וקצר הרי שאכל ג' תבואות וכשיפדנה מוכר יחשוב שנים מיום שמכרה עד היובל אם היו עשר שנים והוא מכרה בעשרה מנים נמצא שמכרה לכל שנה במנה שהרי ביובל היתה עתידה לחזור הלכך כשהוא פודה עכשיו נותן שמנה מנים לשמנה שנים הנותרים וזה אכל שלש תבואות שוות כמה מנים בשתי שנים ואילו הוה אזלינן בתר מנין עולם מתשרי הבאה בשנה האחרת הוה פריק ליה ולא הוה אכיל אלא שתי תבואות:
notes.en: Years of the crops: since it writes “years,” “years of the crops,” why do I need “crops”? Rather, it teaches that every crop he finds in those two years he eats, even three. For instance, if he sold it to him in Nisan, full of standing grain, [the seller] may not redeem it until two years later, in Nisan, on that same day; and if [the buyer] hurried and reaped, he has eaten three crops. When the seller redeems it, he calculates the years from the day he sold it until the Jubilee: if there were ten years and he sold it for ten maneh, it turns out he sold it at a maneh for each year, since at the Jubilee it was going to return. Therefore, when he redeems it now, he gives eight maneh for the eight remaining years, and this one has eaten three crops worth several maneh in two years. Whereas if we followed the world’s count, from Tishrei of the following year he could redeem it, and [the buyer] would have eaten only two crops.

notes.dh: במספר שני תבואות פעמים שאדם אוכל ג' תבואות בב' שנים
notes.he: וא"ת היכי דרשינן מהאי קרא הכי ואימא ד' תבואות לפי ששני משמע שנים ותבואות משמע שנים הרי כאן ארבע וי"ל דדריש ממספר דמשמע שני תבואות וה"ל למכתב תבואה משמע שתבואה אחת יש עדיין וקשה לר"י שאפי' אנו מונין לשנות העולם נמצא ג' תבואות בב' שנים כגון שמכר לו בב' בתשרי שדה מליאה פירות שכשיבא תשרי של שנים הבאים קצר כבר פירותיו מכ"ט באלול וי"ל דשכיח טפי שלשה תבואות בב' שנים שאנו מונין מעת לעת יותר משאנו מונין לבריאת עולם:
notes.en: “According to the number of years of the crops”: sometimes a person eats three crops in two years. And if you ask, how do we expound this from this verse? Say rather four crops, since “years” implies two and “crops” implies two, so there are four! One can answer that it expounds from “number,” which implies [the number of] years [that is, two]; and it should have written “crop” [in the singular]; [writing “crops”] implies that there is one more crop. And Ri found it difficult: even if we count by the years of the world, one finds three crops in two years; for instance, if he sold him a field full of produce on the second of Tishrei, then when Tishrei two years later comes, he has already reaped its produce by the twenty-ninth of Elul. One can answer that three crops in two years are more common when we count from time to time than when we count from the creation of the world.

messages.text: If one purchased a field at the end of the calendar year when its yield had not yet been harvested, and he harvested that yield and subsequently grew and harvested two more crops before the completion of two whole years from the sale, he would have eaten three yields in less than two years. This is not possible if one follows the calendar years, as a new year would start soon after the purchase.

notes.dh: פעמים שאדם אוכל [ג' תבואות בב' שנים]
notes.he: כגון שמכרה לו לפני ר"ה והיא מלאה פירות הרי זה יאכל פירות אלו וזורעה ואוכל ממנה פירות לפני ר"ה אחד [וחוזר] וזורעה ואוכל ממנה פירות עד ר"ה נמצא אוכל ג' תבואות בב' שנים ואי אזלינן בתר שנים של עולם כיון שמכרה לו לפני ר"ה כיון שהגיע ר"ה הבאה נמצאו יוצאות ב' שנים:
notes.en: Sometimes a person eats [three crops in two years]: for instance, he sold it to him before Rosh HaShana when it was full of produce. He eats this produce, sows it and eats produce from it before one Rosh HaShana, [and again] sows it and eats produce from it until [the next] Rosh HaShana; so he eats three crops in two years. Whereas if we followed the years of the world, since he sold it to him before Rosh HaShana, once the next Rosh HaShana came [and the one after it], the two years would already be over.

messages.text: The halakha that the six years stated with regard to a Hebrew slave is calculated by whole years, not calendar years, is derived from the fact that it is written: “Six years he shall work; and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing”. The word “and” in the phrase: “And in the seventh,” teaches that sometimes it turns out that he shall also work in the seventh calendar year, if six full years have not passed from when he was sold.

verse.he: כִּי תִקְנֶה עֶבֶד עִבְרִי שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים יַעֲבֹד וּבַשְּׁבִעִת יֵצֵא לַחׇפְשִׁי חִנָּם׃
verse.en: When you acquire a male Hebrew slave, he shall serve six years; in the seventh year he shall go free, without payment.

notes.he: הקשה הרר"י בן יום טוב דהא לא שמעינן מהכא אלא מעת לעת של שנה אחרונה אבל מעת לעת של שאר שנים מנלן אימא דל' יום שלפני ר"ה חשיבי שנה והשיב לו רשב"ם דקרא ובשביעית גלי לן אשנה אחרונה והוא הדין לשאר שנים דאזלינן בהו מעת לעת דומיא דהנך דכתיבי:
notes.en: “And in the seventh” he shall also work: Rabbi Y. ben Yom Tov asked: we learn from here only [counting] from time to time for the last year; but from time to time for the other years, from where do we derive it? Say that thirty days before Rosh HaShana count as a year! And the Rashbam answered him that the verse “and in the seventh” revealed this to us about the last year, and the same holds for the other years: we follow from time to time with them, like these others that are written.

notes.he: דמשמע דבשביעית נמי יעבוד דוי"ו מוסיף על ענין ראשון כשקנאו בחצי שנה ראשונה:
notes.en: “Six years he shall work, and in the seventh”: which implies that he also works in the seventh, for the “and” adds to the first matter, when he bought him in the middle of the first year.

messages.text: For example, if he was sold in the month of Nisan, although five years and six months have passed when Tishrei, the first month of the seventh year, arrives, since he has not yet completed six years of service he must work in this seventh calendar year as well, until the day of the month in which he was sold.

The baraita also teaches: The years stated with regard to a son and with regard to a daughter are among these terms calculated from the time at the start of the period to the time at the end of the period. With regard to what halakha is this stated?
messages.quote: with regard to a son and with regard to a daughter

notes.he: שנים האמורים בבן ובבת ולקמן מפ' להו:
notes.en: And those of a son and a daughter: years stated regarding a son and a daughter; and below it explains them.

notes.he: אותו יום ואותה שעה לשנה הבאה ולא אזלינן בתר מנין עולם דכי מטי תשרי ניחשוב ליה שתא:
notes.en: From time to time: that same day and that same hour in the next year; and we do not follow the world’s count, counting it a year when Tishrei arrives.

messages.text: With regard to valuations, i.e., that the age of a valuated male or female is calculated in whole years from the date of their birth, not by calendar years.

notes.he: דלא אזלינן בשנת חמש ועשרים וששים בתר מנין עולם:
notes.en: For valuations: that for the fifth, twentieth and sixtieth years we do not follow the world’s count.

notes.he: ואם תאמר בערכין מנלן דבעינן מעת לעת ופירש ר"י דילפינן ליה מבן חדש דכי היכי דאינו נערך בן חדש אלא אם כן יש לו חדש שלם דלא שייך למימר דאזלינן בתר חדש העולם הכי נמי לכל שאר בן חמש ובן עשרים:
notes.en: For valuations: And if you ask, with valuations, from where do we derive that we require from time to time? Ri explained that we derive it from “a month old”: just as one is not valuated as a month old unless he has a full month, for one cannot say we follow the month of the world, so too for all the others, five years old and twenty years old.

notes.he: חמש שנים ועשרים וששים שנה האמורין בערכין כולן מעת לעת:
notes.en: [For valuations: the five years, twenty and sixty years stated in valuations are all from time to time.]

messages.text: The halakha is stated with regard to the matters taught in the fifth chapter of tractate Nidda, which is called after its opening words: Yotze Dofen, i.e., an animal born by caesarean section. In other words, when a mishna in that chapter, which deals with various matters related to the ages of sons and daughters, mentions years, it means full years, even when it does not state this explicitly.

notes.he: במסכת נדה (דף מה:) בן י"ב שנה נדריו נבדקין בן י"ג נדריו קיימין בת אחת עשרה נדריה נבדקין בת שתים עשרה נדריה קיימין וכן הרבה שנות בן ובת שנינו שם וקאמר הכא דכולהו מעת לעת שנולדו:
notes.en: For the chapter Yotze Dofen: in tractate Nidda (45b): a boy of twelve years, his vows are examined; of thirteen, his vows stand; a girl of eleven, her vows are examined; of twelve, her vows stand. Many years of a son and a daughter are taught there likewise, and it says here that all of them are from time to time from when they were born.

notes.he: דמס' נדה דתנן התם בת ג' שנים ויום אחד בן תשע שנים ויום אחד בת י"א שנה ויום א' בת י"ב שנה ויום א' בן י"ב שנה בן י"ג שנה כל אלו שנים מעת לעת]:
notes.en: For the chapter Yotze Dofen: of tractate Nidda, where we learned: a girl three years and one day old, a boy nine years and one day old, a girl eleven years and one day, a girl twelve years and one day, a boy twelve years, a boy thirteen years. All these years are from time to time.

messages.caption: The baraita’s periods counted from time to time, not by the calendar year, and the verse that shows it for each.

messages.text: @Rav Yosef Do you and Rav dispute this matter, i.e., when you apply the mention of a son and a daughter to different cases, do each of you reject the opinion of the other?

notes.he: את ורב גידל דאת לא סברת דרב גידל:
notes.en: Do you dispute: you and Rav Giddel, so that you do not hold like Rav Giddel?

messages.text: @Abaye No, we do not disagree; I said one matter and he said one different matter.

notes.he: לא פליגינן אנא אמרי משמיה דרב חדא והוא אמר חדא:
notes.en: We do not dispute: I said one thing in Rav’s name, and he said one thing.

messages.text: This too stands to reason, as if it enters your mind that they disagree on this matter, then with regard to the one who says full years are required for determining valuations, does he not also say that full years are used for the halakhot of Yotze Dofen?

But doesn’t Rav say, like Rav Yosef, that the halakha in that entire chapter is that the ages of the sons and daughters are determined from the time at the start of the period to the time at the end of the period, not by calendar years?

notes.he: התם במסכת נדה (דף מז:):
notes.en: But doesn’t Rav say: there, in tractate Nidda (47b).

notes.he: דיוצא דופן מעת לעת:
notes.en: The halakha in the entire chapter: of Yotze Dofen is from time to time.

messages.text: But if that is the case, then according to the one who says that the reference to full years mentioned in the baraita is for determining valuations, i.e., Rav, what is the reason he did not say that the baraita is referring to the halakhot of Yotze Dofen?

notes.he: הואיל וסבירא ליה נמי התם מעת לעת:
notes.en: What is the reason he did not say Yotze Dofen: since he too holds there that it is from time to time.

messages.text: Rav would claim that the years of a son and a daughter in the baraita are similar to these other cases mentioned in the baraita: Just as those numbers of years are explicitly written in the Torah, so too these years of the sons and daughters are referring to matters where the years are written in the Torah, i.e., the years of valuations, unlike the topics discussed in Yotze Dofen, where the years are not mentioned expressly in the Torah.

notes.he: אמר לך אפי' הכי הכא לא קתני להו דומיא דהנך שנה דקדשים ודעבד עברי קתני דכתיבי באורייתא והנהו שנים דיוצא דופן כולהו דרבנן:
notes.en: He would tell you: even so, it does not teach them here, for it teaches [cases] similar to these, the year of consecrated animals and of a Hebrew slave, which are written in the Torah; while those years of Yotze Dofen are all rabbinic.

notes.he: דבתי ערי חומה ושדה אחוזה ועבד עברי [וערכין] כתיבי בתורה בפירוש:
notes.en: Similar to these: houses of walled cities, an ancestral field, a Hebrew slave [and valuations], which are written explicitly in the Torah.

messages.text: And with regard to the other, Rav Yosef, how would he respond to this contention? He would maintain that if it enters your mind that the baraita is referring to the years of valuations, which are written in the Torah, then this phrase in the baraita: With regard to a son and with regard to a daughter, is unsuitable.

notes.he: משום דכתיבה קא מרבי לערכין:
notes.en: If it enters your mind: that it includes valuations because they are written.

messages.text: Continues on 19a: had the baraita meant valuations, it should have said “with regard to the male and with regard to the female,” the Torah’s terms for valuations; “son” and “daughter” are the terms used in Yotze Dofen.
